content:
The test image shows a whole-plant view with severely stunted corn plants in the foreground/middle, dramatically shorter than healthy plants behind them. Some appear to have multiple tillers/shoots. Dry soil conditions visible.

From the whole_plant candidates, top suspects: **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** (severe stunting, shortened internodes, tillering), **Crazy_Top** (stunted, bushy appearance, tillering), **Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus** (stunting of upper internodes).

The reference image for Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows dried/dead plants with pinkish leaf discoloration — late-stage disease. The test image shows actively growing green plants that are severely stunted (roughly 1/3 the height of healthy plants nearby), with what appears to be multiple short tillers/stalks growing from single root systems.

Key observations from test image:
- Whole-plant severe stunting (drastically shorter than healthy plants in same row)
- Multiple tillers/compact bushy growth from base
- Plants still green but compressed
- Dry reddish soil (tropical/subtropical conditions)

This matches **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** description: "severe plant stunting due to shortened internodes... stalks may bear multiple ears... excessive tillering." It also partially matches **Crazy_Top** (excessive tillering, stunting, narrow leaves). The compact multi-tiller appearance with uniform green coloring and shortened internodes (plants look "squished" vertically) points more to Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma.
